experiment.title: FNSPID development outcome and label sensitivities
experiment.objective: Test whether the development negative-share association is an artefact of the next-open SPY-adjusted window or the hard FinBERT boundary.

fnspid_price_archive.price_field: adjusted_close = adj close; close-to-close on the SPY calendar

french_daily_ff3.source: Kenneth R. French Data Library daily FF3, decimals, 2009-01-01 through 2020-02-28

ff3.beta_information: returns completed by close of formation session t only
ff3.residual_session: close t to close t+1 using factor realisations on t+1

tests.name: open_soft_negative_mass
tests.soft_negative_mass: n^{-1} sum p_ijt(negative); not added to AGGREGATOR_NAMES

baseline_excluded_from_family.name: headline_open_hard_share
baseline_excluded_from_family.role: predeclared Notebook 71 specification, reported beside the family

estimand.unit: daily cross-sectional coefficient followed by a time-series mean
controls: within-session centred percentile rank of mean_continuous
within-session centred percentile rank of log(1 + n)
estimand.inference: OLS intercept on daily coefficients with Newey-West HAC lag 5
estimand.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg q=0.05 across the three post-hoc coefficients only

claim_boundaries: These three tests were specified after the primary next-open hard-share result was seen. They are not independent confirmation.
Close-to-close starts at the assigned session close, so it is not the executable open-to-open window used by H3.
FF3 residuals use close-to-close French factors. They do not justify a trading or causal claim.
Soft negative mass is computed without a human label audit. Agreement or disagreement with hard share is a measurement note, not a semantic validation.
Do not add soft mass to the original nine-rule family. Do not execute Notebook 75. Do not pool FNSPID with LSEG.
